sections.label: Rare disease patient numbers
sections.summary: From 1992 to 2005, 127 patients were diagnosed, and one estimate suggested 2,000 to 3,000 rare disease patients in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: From 1992 to 2005, a total of 127 patients were diagnosed, although the tests offered did not encompass all known rare diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: One estimate by patient advocacy group Rainbow Across Borders reported in The Straits Times suggests there could be 2,000 to 3,000 rare disease patients in Singapore.

sections.label: Enzyme replacement therapy cost
sections.summary: Alglucosidase alpha, FDA-approved since 2006, reduces risk of death in children by 79% to 95%, and can cost $10,000 a week.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Yet, if patients are given enzyme replacement therapy with alglucosidase alpha, a treatment approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the United States (US) since 2006, there is a significant reduction in the risk of death of such children of between 79% and 95% reduction in the risk of death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It has been reported that it can cost as much as $10,000 a week to treat a young child.

sections.label: MOH support for rare diseases
sections.summary: Rare diseases sometimes do not fit existing policies, and the speaker proposes MOH look at extending more support to children with rare diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And when a condition is very unusual, like a rare disease, it sometimes does not fit easily into existing policies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, what I propose, Mr Deputy Speaker, is for MOH to look at how the Government can extend more support to children with rare diseases.

sections.label: Pooling risk and MOH coverage
sections.summary: Sharing and pooling risk means no Singaporean walks alone, and MOH should find ways to better support children with rare, catastrophic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is part of a broader social policy message that when we share risk, when we pool risk, it means no Singaporean has to walk alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And just as MOH has, over the years, improved coverage for rare, catastrophic illnesses, we can and should find ways to better support children with rare diseases – diseases which are also rare and catastrophic.

sections.label: Insurers denying rare disease coverage
sections.summary: Private insurers limit or deny coverage for pre-existing conditions like rare diseases present from birth, and the Government has a role where the free market is inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In practice, this means private insurance companies limiting or even denying coverage to people with pre-existing conditions, especially rare diseases which are present from birth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Again, Mr Deputy Speaker, we see a role for the Government stepping in where the free market is inadequate, or where no private sector player can find a compelling, commercial case to support such patients.

sections.label: Monthly treatment cost
sections.summary: Combined with consultations and tests, the monthly cost of her treatment adds up to more than $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Combined with other aspects of her treatment, such as consultations and tests, the monthly cost adds up to more than $50,000.

sections.label: Emily's reduced healthcare expenses
sections.summary: After discussing her situation with the hospital, her employer helped her claim part of her treatment cost from group insurance, reducing monthly expenses from over $50,000 to under $500.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: More recently, after discussing her situation with the hospital, her employer helped her to claim part of her treatment cost from their group insurance policy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: So, through the combined efforts by CGH, the pharmaceutical company and her employer, Emily’s monthly healthcare expenses were reduced from more than $50,000 to less than $500.

sections.label: Chloe's reduced healthcare expenses
sections.summary: Together, these helped reduce Chloe's healthcare expenses from $40,000 per month to less than $500 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Together, these helped to reduce Chloe’s healthcare expenses from $40,000 per month to less than $500 a month.

sections.label: MOH review for rare disease children
sections.summary: MOH will review support for children with rare diseases, studying insurance, discretionary funds and a separate fund, with a proposal later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MOH will review how we can better support children with rare diseases and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are studying different options, including the use of insurance and discretionary funds, like MediFund and Medication Assistance Fund, to reduce their out-of-pocket expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Another possibility is to set up a separate fund which our public healthcare institutions can use on a discretionary basis to help children with rare diseases whose treatment costs remain unaffordable in spite of subsidies, insurance and financial assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Contributions to the fund can be made by the Government but also by companies, charities, community groups and individual donors, to encourage different stakeholders in society to chip in and help these families and help these patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Ministry will study the different options carefully and we will come up with a proposal later this year.
